text:
Maria G: Heads up — we need to finalize routing policy behavior for free/pro/enterprise today. Proposal: per-tier routing profiles with ordered model_variant fallback + region preference. Thoughts?

Tom H: +1 on per-tier profiles. Question: should quota exhaustion do reject, fallback, or queue? each has different UX/cost implications.

Sanjay R: For free tier I vote reject or cheap fallback. We shouldn't silently queue free requests (cost shock). For enterprise we can queue or failover to smaller variant.

Lisa K: Thinking about enforcement: gateway should check API key -> tier -> policy. Gateway attempts primary model, if node capacity or quota exhausted then try fallback order. If all fallbacks fail and policy is "queue" then return 202 and queue for reserved capacity.

Tom H: Implementation note: need atomic quota decrement and per-request routing decision to avoid double-serving. Gateway should call account service cache (short TTL) not an RPC per request.

Oliver P: We should surface fallback events in the console and telemetry: fallback_count, fallback_by_variant, fallback_latency, and quota_exhausted_count per region/tier. That will help tune defaults.

Maria G: UX for console: under Settings -> Routing -> Tier policies. Each tier has: priority list of model variants, region preference list, quota_action (reject|fallback|queue), and rollout config. UI should show estimated cost delta for using fallback variants.

Sanjay R: Sample config sketch:
```
policy {
  tiers {
    free {
      primary: "redwood-small-v1-quant"
      fallback: ["redwood-small-v1", "open-alpha-7b"]
      quota_action: "reject"
    }
    pro {
      primary: "redwood-medium-v2"
      fallback: ["redwood-small-v1-quant"]
      quota_action: "fallback"
    }
    enterprise {
      primary: "redwood-large-v1"
      fallback: ["redwood-medium-v2", "redwood-small-v1-quant"]
      quota_action: "queue"
    }
  }
  region_preference: ["us-west-2","eu-central-1"]
}
```

Lisa K: Small API debate: do we attach policy to the API key (token) or to the tenant record? If per-token, customers can create tokens with different tiers which might be useful for subteams. If per-tenant easier to reason about pricing and auditing.

Tom H: I'd prefer tenant-level default plus token-level override for edge cases. Gateway evaluation order: token override -> tenant policy -> global default. Keep policy inheritance simple.

Maria G: Rollout UX: allow canary by percentage of traffic and by account list. Also require guardrails: if fallback_rate > 5% or normalized latency increase > 15% in canary window, auto-rollback.

Oliver P: Telemetry events to add: 
- routing.attempt.{variant} (tags: tier, region, api_key_hash)
- routing.fallback.count (tags: from_variant,to_variant,tier,region)
- routing.quota.exhausted (tags: tier,region)
- routing.action_taken (values: served, fallbacked, queued, rejected)
These let us build per-route dashboards and SLA rollup.

Sanjay R: For quota checks we need strong counters per-tenant with fast path in the gateway. Two-phase approach: keep local token-bucket with periodic sync to central counters; use central only for large commits (monthly billing reconciliation).

Lisa K: Security/audit: every automatic fallback event should be logged with decision reason. Console should have an "Explain route decision" button that shows the chain (tier->primary->failure reason->fallback chosen).

Tom H: Edge case: model variant compatibility. Some fallbacks change response format (e.g., non-deterministic tokenization). We should have model compatibility tags and only fallback to compatible variants or run a lightweight post-processor.

Maria G: Action items:
- @Sanjay R: draft gateway quota cache design and failure modes (due EOD Fri).
- @Lisa K: mockups for Tier policy UI with cost delta and explainers (due Tue).
- @Tom H: write gateway evaluation order & pseudocode for token/tenant/default plus fallback loop.
- @Oliver P: list telemetry metrics + Grafana dashboard wireframe (due Mon).

DeployBot: Policy change branch pushed to staging: refs/heads/routing-tier-policies (CI: green) :rocket:

Maria G: Thanks everyone — we'll review in tomorrow sync and pick defaults.
